_comment: forest: Map 3. Authored in WORLD coordinates, instance at identity: grass lane r 46.7..57.3 at y 23.0 (as map 1), the pit bank down to a dark floor at y -11.05 (r 42) under the fog, a leaf wall from r 57.3 up to the gallery roof at y 36, a cell wall of six barred tiers from y 36 to y 64 on its inner rim, and an UNBROKEN canopy dome from y 64 to y 77.4 over the ravine (no holes: the sun shafts come down through the closed leaves, starting just under the surface), hanging leaf clumps under the sun-wells, 12 forest trunks standing in the wall, two tiers of cells with branch bars cut into the wall and 36 into the pit bank, a thicket of thorny brambles out of the pit floor rising from the fog, ferns and hummocks along the wall foot and the lip only. TWELVE surfaces on ForestGround, one tiling sheet per class through lib/texel.py (grass, verge, path, edge, leaf, shade, sun, fern, bark, earth, cell, root), world-projected at 0.05 m per texel, no atlas windows. ForestRaysSolid and ForestRaysSoft are the sun-ray shafts (one per sun-well, three crossed vanes, same geometry, tint and feather in COLOR_0, pale / faint) behind MESH_RAYS, one surface each. ForestFog is the pit's fog: stacked translucent discs, tint and alpha in COLOR_0, one surface (GL Compatibility has no fog volumes). ForestCollision is the purpose-built collider shipped as a `-colonly` node (flat lane, pit cone, pit floor, flat wall r 57.3, flat ceiling annulus y 36); Godot turns it into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `surfaces` counts only what is drawn.
